summary.text: 45-year-old man with von Zumbusch-type generalized pustular psoriasis diagnosed at age 20, admitted during a 2005 flare-up with generalized tiny pustules, erythema and fever; cyclosporine, methotrexate and acitretin did not prevent recurrent exacerbations.

From June 2017 he took secukinumab 300 mg (baseline, weeks 1-4, then monthly) with daily acitretin 25 mg, and his lesions changed to annular hyperkeratotic plaques with marginal pustules; his condition stayed stable until secukinumab was stopped in July 2023.
A flare-up in November 2023 showed well-demarcated poly-annular pustular plaques without fever or fatigue, and skin biopsy confirmed pustular psoriasis.

Secukinumab was introduced on day 14 of his admission with significant improvement, pustules subsiding and plaques resolving within 1 week; he was discharged with outpatient follow-up and on monthly secukinumab 300 mg had complete clearance for 18 months.

ambiguities.issue: The text states an admission during a 2005 flare-up and later a November 2023 flare-up, then says secukinumab was introduced on day 14 of "his admission" without naming the admission. The Figure 1B caption calls the 2017 dose the first dose and the drug was continued until July 2023, so the introduction follows that discontinuation; the text never states the admission date or that the biopsy belongs to it.
ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not assign a calendar date to the day-14 introduction or to the biopsy, and do not state that the biopsy was performed during that admission.

evidence.quote: The pustules subsided, and skin plaques began desquamating with resolution within a time span of 1 week

ambiguities.issue: The 1-week resolution and later 18-month clearance follow the day-14 secukinumab start but no calendar dates are given for them.
ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not assign calendar dates to discharge or the 18-month clearance period.

ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not copy cited-case findings or treatments to this patient.

caption_evidence.quote: Generalized tiny pustules with erythema (A). Multiple erythematous, annular shape‐like hyperkeratotic plaques with pustules along the edges after the first dose of Secukinumab (B). Multiple poly‐annular and circular pattern pustular plaques, presenting typical annular pustular psoriasis lesions after cessation of Secukinumab (C) and (D). Biopsy from the trunk showed psoriasiform acanthosis, parakeratosis, and proliferated vessels in dermal papillae with inflammatory infiltration (hematoxylin–eosin stain, original magnification ×40) (E). Subcorneal neutrophilic microabscesses (hematoxylin–eosin stain, original magnification ×40) (F). Annular pustular plaque subsided with post‐inflammatory pigmentation after Secukinumab prescription (G).

Discussion cites other published pustular psoriasis patients (Liao, Khosravi-Hafshejani, Herrero-Moyano); they are not facts about this patient.
